column4: (3)  No  person  shall,  without  prior  written  approval  of

column3: the  Authority,  import,  sell  or  distribute  any  medicine  to
the  general  public  as  a  treatment,  prevention  or  cure  for
any  of  the  prescribed  diseases,  disorders  or  abnormal
physical states.

column4: (1) Every Medical Practitioner, Dentist or Veterinary

column3: Surgeon  shall  write  the  generic  name  of  the  medicine  in
every prescription issued by him.

column4: (2) Where the Medical Practitioner, Dentist or Veterinary

column3: Surgeon so requires, he may in addition to the generic name
write  a  particular  brand  name  of  the  medicine  in  the
prescription.

column4: (3)  A  Medical  Practitioner,  Dentist  or  Veterinary

column3: Surgeon  may  write  only  the  brand  name  of  a  medicine  in
the  prescription  where  the  medicine  prescribed  is  a
combined  medicine  for  which  the  generic  name  is  not
available.

column4: (4) Where the brand name of the medicines, which is in

column3: the prescription is not available or affordable to the customer,
the  Pharmacist  may  dispense  any  other  generic  medicine
with the consent of the customer.

column4: (5) The Pharmacist shall inform the customer the range of

column3: generic medicines with or without brand names available in
the Pharmacy and their prices enabling the customer to buy
the medicine according to his choice.

column4: (6)  A  Pharmacist  who  fails  to  disclose  the  generic

column3: medicines  with  or  without  brand  names  available  in    the
Pharmacy and their prices to the customer at the time of sale,
commits an offence.

column4: Any person who contravenes any of the provisions

column3: specified in this Part of this Act commits an offence.
